Hello, everyone. I am Shruti from the Partner Enablement team at Leizer. In this video, we will have a brief walk-through of what Leizer is all about. Let's say you are getting into the agentic world. You start by building a simple agent, and then you realize how powerful agents are, and you start building agents.
Slowly, you want memory for the agents, then comes the rag, then comes integration with multiple tools, putting together the guardrails so that the agents can be safely deployed to production, putting together the testing framework for the agent, observability for the agent, and soon you realize there are lots of different pieces that are just out of your control.
And that is where Leizer is your friend. It is a one-stop shop for managing the complete agent life cycle At Lysa, we help enterprises reimagine their complex workflows with agentic AI automation. Let's see some of the examples as to how Lysa has helped clients. So we have multiple clients across the globe, and our mission is to take the workloads from being people native to being agent native.
So here is an example of how we have helped WTW put together a retirement advisory solution. Yet another example that we have is for Accenture, where we have put together a corporate venture capital function for them, and now they have Agentic OS running two hundred plus agents, multiple functions, and it has just made their life very easy Here is yet another example of how we have helped KPMG to put together their procurement lifecycle solutions
Now that you already know that it can put together multiple different types of solutions, let us see how the Laiza stack is put together. At the bottommost layer of the stack is the infrastructure layer.  The infrastructure layer specifies where all Laiza can be deployed.
It can be deployed on any of the cloud providers, be it Azure, AWS, or GCP. It can also be deployed on on-prem solutions like bare metal, virtual machines. On top of this infrastructure layer is the integration layer with multiple models and third-party tools. As an agent, it needs to have a model that powers the agent as well as it needs to interact with different third-party tools.
All of this integration is taken care of at this layer. Then comes the agent framework, the layer which takes care of how to develop and deploy the agents. And then comes the Laiza agent studio layer. This is the layer which interacts directly with the client. You as the user of Laiza will be working on the agent studio in order to develop agents, in order to put together the knowledge base and integrate the tools.
All of this will be done by the client or by the user at this layer. And then the topmost layer is architect. This is the white coding platform on which you can put to- out your thoughts as to what you want to build, and the architect takes care of building that application for you completely. It puts together a very nice front end with an agentic back end, and you get a working application right out of the box So together, the stack has five layers, and we will look at the Architect and the Studio.
So, as I mentioned, Architect is the most sophisticated layer where you can just put out your thoughts as to what type of application you want to build. The Architect puts together a detailed document explaining what it is going to build, the type of UI that it is going to have, as well as the different agents that it is going to create in order to power the front end.
Once you are happy with the plan, you can proceed, and it will actually create the agents in Studio. Once the agents are created, it will create a front end that will be powered by this agentic backend
If you don't want to use Architect and create the agents yourself, Studio is your go-to place. It's a SaaS solution offering that Lysa has, where users can come and in a low-code fashion can put together their agents. This is the home screen of Lysa Studio. Whatever you can do on Lysa Studio in the form of UI interaction can also be done using API endpoints, or it can also be coded using Lysa SDK
Everything that you need to build agentic AI at scale is supported by Leiser. You can put together a simple agent, or you can make it a complex workflow, be it a managerial workflow or a predetermined workflow. Also, you can build voice agents. You can integrate your agents with knowledge base. You can have guardrails associated with your agents.
you can put in memory models, not just the commercial models, but also your pre-trained models can be integrated with the agents. Leiser also comes in with a very sophisticated testing framework for evals
So without Lysa, you have multiple solutions which solves one part of this puzzle. But with Lysa, you get all the offerings at one place. You have support across different models, be it any commercial model, or you can also bring in your own model. You can integrate with multiple third-party tools, MCP servers, and skills.
You can put together RAG in multiple formats. It could be a simple RAG, or it could be a knowledge graph. Also, it has very rich support for guardrails, wherein you can put together any compliance policy, and it's just supported seamlessly by Lysa   This is yet another way in which you can see how Lieser has been put together. The bottommost layer specifies the infra layer, and you can see that multiple cloud providers are supported by Lieser. it also supports bare metal and virtual machine, so it can be deployed seamlessly on on-prem infra as well.
Then it supports multiple models. It could be commercial models, or it could also be your pre-trained models, which you can host at different locations. And then on top of these two layers is where your agent functions. You build your agent, integrate with multiple different stuffs like RAG, tools, skills, have hallucination manager in place, have agentic app builder, tool integrator, memory manager.
All of this has been put together as one solution by Lieser
Let us take a little closer look at how your agent is functioning behind the scene. So if you look at it, whatever data comes in from the left is first filtered by your responsible and safe AI layer. If there is any PII data, it can be redacted. There is a toxicity check, a prompt injection check, and an agent entitlement.
Only after these checks, the input goes to the agent CPU. The agent then interacts with the LLM, with the RAG, with the tools, and whatever output is generated is again sent to the hallucination manager and responsible safe AI layer. After that, the loop continues, uh, to the feedback, back to the agent till you get a satisfactory final result.
And only when you have the final output that it goes into the output processing layer. That means it is going to multiple places like in the memory, so that your further conversations have context of the interactions that you have had with the agent, and then to the agent eval for testing purposes and to the agent REST for observability.
And once the output has made to these places, it is given out to you as a user
So now that we have seen the lighter offerings in the form of Studio and Architect, we also have one other solution for you, which is Computer Agent. As a computed agent, you can bring your own open gap, that is your agent present in the form of files on GitHub or on GitLab, and then you can bring your own harness, you can bring your own runtime.
That is where the agent is supposed to run. You can bring your own memory, and then you can have this agent put out the output to any of the communication channels. So Computer Agent is yet another powerful framework that we have brought to the world And last but not the least, we have Git agent.
One of the offerings of Lysate which has become really famous. 
Git Agent is a Git native multimodal AI agent harness. Here, the agent definition lies entirely in the Git repository.
Be it the agent's role, goal, and instructions, the tools that the agent is integrated with, the model, the skills, all of it lies as files in the Git repository. The Git agent can be installed with a simple command, and then it can run this particular agent, which is present in the Git repository
That's a brief about Lysr and the different offerings that Lysr has.
Thank you
